key_holding: Publishers, editors, reporters, and persons connected with news media CANNOT be held in contempt for refusing to disclose (1) the source of any information procured for publication or broadcast, or (2) any unpublished information obtained in gathering news. Operates at two levels: statutory (§1070) and constitutional (Art. I §2(b), added 1980).

case_law.case: O'Grady v. Superior Court (Apple Computer, Inc.), 139 Cal.App.4th 1423 (2006)
case_law.rule: Shield law extends to online publishers. A person who gathers information for communication to the public through an online publication is protected regardless of medium. No subject-matter exception for trade secrets.
